title: Intro to BREAD
text: Many methylation studies purely discovery-oriented. Instead asking “CpGs significant genome-wide?”, question often region-centric: bivalent promoters hypermethylated tumor vs. normal? PMD-like heterochromatin regions lose methylation aging? predefined chromatin classes show coherent change? BREAD answers questions directly, returning posterior probabilities per region biologically meaningful effect-size threshold.

what: A real-data demo: TCGA matched tumor–normal (HM450)
title: Intro to BREAD
text: use HM450.76.TCGA.matched sesameData — 10,042 HM450 probes × 76 samples (38 patients matched Normal + Tumour). strong, well-understood signal: tumors show broad hypermethylation Polycomb targets hypomethylation partially-methylated / quiescent regions.
code: library(BREAD) library(sesameData) library(knowYourCG) library(SummarizedExperiment) library(GenomicRanges) library(ggplot2) library(patchwork) tcga      <- sesameData::sesameDataGet("HM450.76.TCGA.matched") probeInfo <- sesameData::sesameDataGet("HM450.probeInfo") probes <- probeInfo$mapped.probes.hg38 # keep only probes present in the TCGA beta matrix keep   <- intersect(rownames(tcga$betas), names(probes)) se <- SummarizedExperiment(   assays    = list(betas = tcga$betas[keep, , drop = FALSE]),   rowRanges = probes[keep],   colData   = tcga$sampleInfo ) se$type <- factor(se$type, levels = c("Normal", "Tumour")) se #> class: RangedSummarizedExperiment  #> dim: 9850 76  #> metadata(0): #> assays(1): betas #> rownames(9850): cg00076353 cg00105628 ... ch.20.61946943R #>   ch.20.1527371F #> rowData names(0): #> colnames(76): 2671-Tumour 2675-Tumour ... 6322-Normal 6625-Normal #> colData names(2): patient type

title: Intro to BREAD
text: use KnowYourCG’s HM450 chromHMM database group probes chromatin state, merge nearby -state probes intervals. gives us biologically meaningful feature classes manual annotation work.
code: chromhmm <- knowYourCG::getDBs("KYCG.HM450.chromHMM.20211020") #> Selected the following database groups: #> 1. KYCG.HM450.chromHMM.20211020 # chromhmm is a named list: state -> character vector of probe IDs str(chromhmm, list.len = 3, give.attr = FALSE) #> List of 15 #>  $ 5_TxWk     : chr [1:50090] "cg13869341" "cg09989996" "cg11954957" "cg20788133" ... #>  $ 15_Quies   : chr [1:136838] "cg14008030" "cg12045430" "cg20826792" "cg00381604" ... #>  $ 1_TssA     : chr [1:124275] "cg10037654" "cg14057946" "cg11422233" "cg16047670" ... #>   [list output truncated]  # Keep a few interpretable classes state_map <- c(   BivProm   = "10_TssBiv",   ReprPC    = "13_ReprPC",   ActiveTSS = "1_TssA",   Enh       = "7_Enh" ) state_probes <- chromhmm[names(chromhmm) %in% state_map] # Rename to friendly labels names(state_probes) <- names(state_map)[match(names(state_probes), state_map)]  # Build regions per class: intersect with our SE probes, merge by ±2 kb features <- do.call(c, unname(lapply(names(state_probes), function(cls) {   pids <- intersect(state_probes[[cls]], rownames(se))   if (length(pids) < 3L) return(GRanges())   gr  <- rowRanges(se)[pids]   red <- GenomicRanges::reduce(GenomicRanges::resize(gr, 4001L, fix = "center"))   ov  <- GenomicRanges::countOverlaps(red, gr)   red <- red[ov >= 3L]   # Cap per class for speed   if (length(red) > 120L) red <- sort(red[sample.int(length(red), 120L)])   mcols(red)$feature_class <- cls   names(red) <- sprintf("%s_%03d", cls, seq_along(red))   red }))) table(features$feature_class) #>  #> ActiveTSS   BivProm       Enh    ReprPC  #>       120        22        35       119

title: Intro to BREAD
text: fit_bread() auto-detects assay ("betas") scale ("Beta" value range), minimal call : hood BREAD running analytic conjugate posterior per region; 480 regions fit well second laptop. Default thresholds (delta = 0.10, prob_cutoff = 0.95) can overridden want stricter looser.
code: fit <- fit_bread(se, features, design = ~ type,                  feature_class_col = "feature_class") #> `contrast` not supplied; using 'typeTumour' (first non-intercept coefficient). fit #> <BreadFit> #>   mode       : summary  #>   backend    : conjugate  #>   input_scale: Beta  #>   assay      : betas  #>   contrast   : typeTumour  #>   delta      : 0.1  #>   prob_cutoff: 0.95  #>   n_regions  : 296 (of  296  input) #>   classifications: #>     hypermethylated  126 #>     hypomethylated   34 #>     inconclusive     136

title: Intro to BREAD
text: region r, default backend fits conjugate Normal–Inverse-Gamma regression region-level mean beta (transformed M): yir∼𝒩(Xiβr,σr2),βr∣σr2∼𝒩(μ0,σr2Λ0−1),σr2∼Inv-Gamma(a0,b0). y_{ir} \sim \mathcal{N}(X_i\beta_r,\ \sigma_r^2),\quad \beta_r\mid\sigma_r^2 \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_0,\ \sigma_r^2\Lambda_0^{-1}),\quad \sigma_r^2 \sim \text{Inv-Gamma}(a_0, b_0). marginal posterior contrast coefficient location–scale Student-t df = 2 a_n. BREAD uses pt()/qt() compute P(β>δ)P(\beta > \delta) P(β<−δ)P(\beta < -\delta) analytically — MCMC. classification rule : hypermethylated P(β>δ)≥P(\beta > \delta) \geprob_cutoff, hypomethylated P(β<−δ)≥P(\beta < -\delta) \geprob_cutoff, inconclusive otherwise. Need partial pooling across regions, non-conjugate priors, ordered contrasts? Set backend = "brms"; everything else stays .

title: BREAD on real EPICv2 data: vitamin C in serially passaged fibroblasts
text: Ascorbic acid (vitamin C) cofactor TET dioxygenases, oxidize 5mC → 5hmC → 5fC → 5caC drive active DNA demethylation. TET activity thought protect CpG islands aberrant age-associated hypermethylation. serially passaged human fibroblasts, two CpG sets consistently change: PRC-CGI (Polycomb-marked CpG islands, H3K27me3 ∩ CGI) gain methylation passage number; PMD-soloWCGW (late-replicating solo-WCGW CpGs within partially methylated domains) lose methylation passage number. question experiment asks: VitC supplementation attenuate either signal? conventional probe-level DMP pipeline reports significant CpGs; BREAD asks complementary, region-centric question directly: predefined feature region, posterior probability methylation effect exceeds biologically meaningful threshold?

title: BREAD on real EPICv2 data: vitamin C in serially passaged fibroblasts
text: BREAD ships small (~0.5 MB) subset real EPICv2 experiment lab — 8 arrays AG06561 fetal skin fibroblasts across 2 × 2 design (condition × passage × 2 technical replicates). data-raw builder data-raw/make_vitc_extdata.R (source repository). Five feature classes, 100 regions , autosomes, region spanning ≥ 3 EPICv2 probes ±2 kb merge. reg$feature_class drive plot_feature_set() stratification .
code: library(BREAD) library(SummarizedExperiment) library(GenomicRanges) library(ggplot2) library(patchwork)  se  <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "vitc_ag06561.rds", package = "BREAD")) reg <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "vitc_regions.rds", package = "BREAD")) se #> class: RangedSummarizedExperiment  #> dim: 6716 8  #> metadata(0): #> assays(1): betas #> rownames(6716): cg00003513 cg00004633 ... cg27639620 cg27642771 #> rowData names(7): Probe_ID CpG_Island ... text: n = 2 per arm. credible intervals wide many regions remain inconclusive. BREAD’s posterior probabilities honest answer given data; lowering prob_cutoff , say, 0.80 promote regions hyper / hypo also admit false positives. Technical replicates, biological. Real variance aa57 effect across fibroblast lines captured experiment produce additional dispersion included. Feature-class regions constructed EPICv2 manifest’s probe-level annotations (CGI, PMD, histone marks) merging nearby annotated probes. Users consider higher-resolution external references (ENCODE chromHMM, segway, compartment-aware WGBS-derived PMD calls) question demands .

title: Fit BREAD summary-mode Bayesian model — fit_bread_summary
text: list : fits: per-region list list(mu_n, Lambda_n_inv, a_n, b_n, n, error) design_matrix: model matrix X actually used coef_names: coefficient names contrast, contrast_idx: contrast name column index X region_ids: rownames region_mat prior: prior applied (mu0/Lambda0 filled )

title: Fit BREAD summary-mode Bayesian model — fit_bread_summary
text: region r sample : $$y_{ir} \sim \mathcal{N}(X_i \beta_r,\, \sigma_r^2),$$ $$\beta_r \mid \sigma_r^2 \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_0,\, \sigma_r^2 \Lambda_0^{-1}),$$ $$\sigma_r^2 \sim \mathrm{Inv\text{-}Gamma}(a_0, b_0).$$ Posterior: $$\Lambda_n = X^\top X + \Lambda_0,\quad \mu_n = \Lambda_n^{-1}(X^\top y + \Lambda_0 \mu_0),$$ $$a_n = a_0 + n/2,\quad b_n = b_0 + \tfrac{1}{2}(y^\top y + \mu_0^\top \Lambda_0 \mu_0 - \mu_n^\top \Lambda_n \mu_n).$$
